claims.hypothesis: Are the nuclear dust disks warm and optically thick at 434 um?
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits and flux-ratio solutions combining ALMA 691 GHz with 345 and 230 GHz data
claims.result: West: T_D~200 K, tau=5.3; East: ~80 K, tau=1.7
claims.finding: The western nucleus is warmer and more opaque than the eastern

evidence.quote: The western nucleus is revealed to contain warm (200 K) dust that is optically thick

claims.hypothesis: Does the western nucleus luminosity surface density require an AGN or hot starburst?
claims.experiment: Computed sigma T^4 from size and T_D
claims.result: log = 14.3, excludes ordinary starburst at ~3 sigma but depends on geometry
claims.finding: AGN or hot starburst needed, though uncertain

evidence.quote: the luminosity surface density of the western nucleus excludes a starburst solution at the $\sim 3\sigma$ level, the derived values depend heavily on the poorly resolved geometry of the source.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Uniform elliptical disk model gives lower temperatures (55 K east, 79 K west)

evidence.quote: the dust temperatures are somewhat lower (55 K for the eastern nucleus and 79 K for the western nucleus)

limitations_admitted.value: Western nucleus poorly resolved along beam major axis; minor axis unknown

evidence.loc: Optical depth, source size, and dust temperature
evidence.quote: The western nucleus is not well resolved along the beam major axis, with a deconvolved diameter just 55% of the beam

referee_caveats_inferred: Results depend strongly on assumed source geometry and the unresolved western minor axis
Flux scale from bandpass calibrator only (15%)
Gas-to-dust and tau/N_H factor of 2 tuned to match dynamical mass
Comparison of different-epoch/different-instrument fluxes assumes matched apertures
